objective: Review the direct sidecar launch authority boundary definition, accept only the future-run authority chain, and select a run gate without claiming direct Verilator sidecar execution, timing, arbitrary filelist support, automatic allocation, runtime/ABI change, raw full-state equality, or production LLM-serving throughput.

review_decision.reason: The definition is narrow enough: a future direct-launch claim must connect one Verilator-facing process parse, explicit pulp_ita_mha 64x1 sidecar context, reviewed stage authority, sidecar launch, and coverage-output compare in one authority chain. It preserves the separation between parser success, wrapper execution, generated command text, stage-plan metadata, and actual launch authority.
review_decision.weakest_point: The boundary is still definition-only. It defines the direct-launch proof shape, but it does not execute a Verilator-facing command through sidecar stages and therefore cannot prove native sidecar launch, timing, arbitrary filelist support, automatic allocation, runtime/ABI change, raw full-state equality, or production throughput.
accepted_because: the source definition uses the first scoped sidecar execution run review as its authority source
the future claim requires a single native invocation record rather than stitching unrelated evidence together after the fact
parser success, generated command text, wrapper execution, and stage-plan metadata remain non-authoritative
reports and artifacts remain generated evidence only

required_next_gate.name: run_verilator_native_option_parser_direct_command_path_native_invocation_direct_sidecar_launch_gate
must_record: whether a real Verilator-facing process was invoked
whether the expanded native option spelling parsed successfully
whether explicit pulp_ita_mha 64x1 sidecar context was connected to that invocation
whether reviewed stage authority was used before any sidecar stage ran
whether sidecar launch was reached from the native path or failed before launch
whether coverage_output_equivalence compare executed and what mismatch count was observed if compare ran
which failure class applies if the chain does not complete

non_claims: not broad native Verilator option support
not automatic optimal GPU allocation for any design
reports and artifacts are generated evidence, not source of truth
